keyPoints.en: Aim: defend sovereignty, religion, customs and traditional rights. Forms: armed and non-armed.
keyPoints.bm: Matlamat: mempertahankan kedaulatan, agama, adat dan hak tradisional. Bentuk: bersenjata dan tanpa senjata.

keyPoints.en: Chiefs lost tax rights and powers; new taxes and land laws burdened people; customs and religion were ignored.
keyPoints.bm: Pembesar hilang hak cukai dan kuasa; cukai dan undang-undang tanah baharu membebankan rakyat; adat dan agama diabaikan.

keyPoints.en: Dol Said (Naning 1831–32), Maharaja Lela (Perak 1875), Bahaman & Mat Kilau (Pahang 1891–95), Tok Janggut (Kelantan 1915), Abdul Rahman Limbong (Terengganu 1928).
keyPoints.bm: Dol Said (Naning 1831–32), Maharaja Lela (Perak 1875), Bahaman & Mat Kilau (Pahang 1891–95), Tok Janggut (Kelantan 1915), Abdul Rahman Limbong (Terengganu 1928).

keyPoints.en: Sarawak: Rentap, Sharif Masahor. Sabah: Mat Salleh (1894–1900), Antanom (1915).
keyPoints.bm: Sarawak: Rentap, Sharif Masahor. Sabah: Mat Salleh (1894–1900), Antanom (1915).

keyPoints.en: Resistance was crushed; leaders killed or exiled; British control tightened.
keyPoints.bm: Penentangan dipatahkan; pemimpin dibunuh atau dibuang negeri; kawalan British diperketat.

keyPoints.en: It inspired later nationalism; the fighters are remembered as heroes.
keyPoints.bm: Ia menjadi inspirasi nasionalisme kemudian; pejuang dikenang sebagai wira.
